questions.question: Do files and folders share one name namespace among siblings (can a file `a` and a folder `a` coexist)?

options.label: Shared namespace (Recommended)
options.description: Sibling uniqueness over all children, as in your draft. Key is injective with a single rule, and matches POSIX. Cannot represent S3 where `a` and `a/` are distinct objects.

options.label: Separate namespaces
options.description: A file and folder may share a name under one parent. Key then needs a type marker (e.g. trailing '/' for folders) to stay injective; one more axiom and a case split in proofs.

questions.question: May a folder exist while empty, as a first-class entity?

options.label: Yes, folders are first-class (Recommended)
options.description: Folders exist independently of their content. Simplest model; object-store backends must emulate them later. Keeps F and I symmetric.

options.label: No, folders exist only as prefixes
options.description: Axiom: every non-root folder has a descendant item. Matches S3, but deleting the last item implicitly deletes ancestors, pushing complexity into operation semantics.

questions.question: How strict should the name alphabet be beyond non-empty and no '/'?

options.label: Exclude '.', '..' and NUL (Recommended)
options.description: Keeps Key canonical (no `a/./b` aliasing). Case-sensitive, no Unicode normalization: names compare as raw code point sequences.

options.label: Only non-empty and no '/'
options.description: Minimal and purely combinatorial. `.` and `..` are ordinary names; normalization is the caller's problem.

options.label: Abstract Valid(name) predicate
options.description: Name validity is an arbitrary predicate guaranteeing non-empty and no '/'. Most general; proofs use only those guarantees.

questions.question: Finiteness and scope of this first pass?

options.label: Finite, static + Key lemmas (Recommended)
options.description: U finite; axioms, derived parent/depth/Key, and proved lemmas (acyclicity, unique parent, Key injectivity, Key resolution). Operations in a second pass.

options.label: Unrestricted, static + Key lemmas
options.description: No finiteness axiom; well-foundedness only via reachability from root. More general, induction needs the ancestor-chain argument spelled out.

options.label: Finite, static + operations
options.description: Also create/delete/move/copy with pre/postconditions and invariant preservation. Larger and riskier in one pass.

questions.question: Where in sdd/ should the store-model axioms document live?

options.label: Research doc (Recommended)
options.description: sdd/research/research-store-model-axioms.md, dual, directory default, no marker needed. Exploratory and draft-grade, so no spec-ID or test-traceability obligations yet. It can be promoted to a spec or folded into spec 004 once the formalization is done.

options.label: New spec 051
options.description: sdd/specs/051-store-model.md. Becomes source of truth immediately: code vs spec conflicts then resolve against it, and spec/test traceability rules (000-process) apply from day one. Heavy for a draft that is not yet formalized or reconciled with spec 004.

options.label: RFC
options.description: sdd/rfcs/rfc-NNNN-store-model.md. Fits if you want it reviewed and accepted as a proposal before it becomes normative; carries the RFC lifecycle and decision record.

questions.question: Should this work be tracked under a backlog item, with trace and CHANGELOG handling?

options.label: File a new BK item (Recommended)
options.description: Create a backlog entry (and dossier/trace as the repo rules require) so the doc ships under an ID and its commits are prefixed with it. Consistent with the repo's ship-complete principle.

options.label: No item yet
options.description: Write the doc on the branch without an ID, commit messages unprefixed. Faster for now, but the repo expects item-tracked work, so an item would have to be filed before the PR.

questions.question: How should AX-4 be restated, given its existence half follows from AX-6?

options.label: At most one container (Recommended)
options.description: AX-4 becomes uniqueness only; existence is stated as a consequence of AX-6. Makes every axiom independent, so the 'countermodel per axiom' claim becomes true. Changes the axiom wording and the §5 row.

options.label: Keep both halves, drop the independence claim
options.description: AX-4 stays as is, for readability. §5 and the BK-435 entry say independence holds for the uniqueness half only. Smaller edit, weaker 'rock solid' story.

questions.question: How should the comparison section's unverified claims be handled?

options.label: Downgrade and bound them (Recommended)
options.description: Relabel Z and SibylFS as summary only, remove unbounded claims, fix the JSON and flat-store sentences, and mark the Alloy reading as one course's model. No further research.

options.label: Verify against primary sources first
options.description: Fetch the Alloy source, the official ZooKeeper guide, and the Z and Lem specs before rewriting. More accurate, noticeably more work.

questions.question: Which review findings should I apply?

options.label: All confirmed findings (Recommended)
options.description: Math fixes, §5 completions and a richer witness, L5 and L6 wording, §9 corrections, N/A convention, and BK-435 title and trace consistency, then rerun the gates and send it back to the reviewer.

options.label: Math findings only
options.description: Fix findings 1 to 11 now; leave the comparison and convention findings for a later pass.
